diagrams.title: The Orchard content lifecycle
diagrams.summary: How discovery, currency review, owner gates, authoring, release, and live verification form one governed content lifecycle.
diagrams.description: The Orchard joins discovery and currency signals with an explicit request path, owner approval gates, evidence-backed authoring and review, release, and live verification. Dashed nodes distinguish designed work that is not yet implemented from running controls.
diagrams.altText: A governed content lifecycle with discovery, currency, and request-intake lanes feeding owner Gate 1; approved work proceeds through authoring and review to digest-bound Gate 2, commit, release, and live verification, while denials stop delivery or return work for revision.
diagrams.caption: The Orchard keeps discovery, authoring, approval, release, and verification in one evidence-preserving lifecycle.
takeaways: Discovery and currency findings enter one governed queue.
Owner approval gates establish delivery and publication authority.
Designed but unimplemented steps remain visibly distinct from running controls.
